experiment: P5 H4 robust joint-schedule oracle v1
purpose: test whether four-block joint scheduling has material WER headroom beyond the existing blockwise robust utility oracle before training any heatmap temporal model

budget_and_decoder.tail: enumerate the remaining one to three complete blocks as a shorter final horizon; incomplete final block receives skeleton only

blockwise_control.definition: exact reproduction of the existing robust-continuation oracle
blockwise_control.choice: choose a side only when its minimum terminal edit-error improvement versus center is strictly positive; maximize that minimum; tie left then right

joint_h4_oracle.candidate_schedules: all 3^H bonus-offset schedules for H in 1..4
joint_h4_oracle.past: the joint oracle's own previously selected horizons
joint_h4_oracle.reward: for each future separately, terminal edit error of the all-center schedule minus candidate-schedule terminal edit error
joint_h4_oracle.robust_value: minimum reward across the two future continuations
joint_h4_oracle.eligibility: robust_value strictly greater than zero; otherwise select the all-center schedule
tie_break: larger sum of the two rewards

primary_comparisons.joint_h4_vs_blockwise_robust: incremental value of multi-block joint selection

integrity: all three policies have identical selected-window counts per sample
gates.decision: all gates must pass before any H4 schedule predictor or ordered heatmap-U experiment

forbidden: calibration, dev, test, or held-out outcomes
changing horizon, continuations, tie-break, thresholds, or decoder after outcomes
training a predictor before the oracle gates pass
claiming deployability: this oracle reads reference, future continuation, and true sequence endpoint
